body: ASSIGNED: sweep slice 1, embed-core, bd-01M16BFTZNPEP1VAXDGWDBTE4G, P1, now UNBLOCKED - your reference shape landed at 52c2bbe. Everything is pre-scoped on the bead: ten types with exact files and lines, the order within the slice, the shape, and the gate line. Read it before starting; I wrote it so you would not have to re-derive anything. THREE THINGS I WANT TO FLAG. (1) ONE DOOR ONLY - fromProduct. Do not carry forward probes for copy (a private constructor already suppresses it; I verified with a control) or for unapply/_1/_2/Product (read-only, construct nothing, and every field on these ten is public anyway). None of the ten hides a field, so the rule-8 exception does not apply. You over-closed last time and corrected it promptly; this bead already encodes the corrected scope. (2) REFERENCE SCOPE IS COMPUTED, NOT GUESSED: embed-core, embed-bench AND embed-grakern all reference these types, so all three are in the gate - embed-grakern is JVM-only, embed-core is cross-built. That rule exists because it caught the laws failure on your last candidate. (3) START WITH ValidatedVector and demonstrate the forge in one line before you fix it, m1-style. Its of() rejects dimension mismatch, non-finite values, non-normalized vectors and the zero vector - four checks - and if fromProduct does NOT reproduce a NaN or unnormalized vector there, SAY SO LOUDLY: my 45-count would be wrong and I will withdraw it rather than defend it. Your population work was good under a lot of correction, some of which was mine and wrong.
